heart.name: Heart
heart.referenceNote: Shared BodyParts3D adult-male organ reference, opened from either body. This is not a sex-specific organ reconstruction.

structures.name: Right atrium
structures.description: Receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body.

structures.name: Left atrium
structures.description: Receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the lungs.

structures.name: Right ventricular cavity
structures.description: The right ventricle pumps blood toward the lungs. This mesh represents its cavity boundary, not its muscular wall.

structures.name: Left ventricular cavity
structures.description: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta. This mesh represents its cavity boundary, not its muscular wall.

structures.name: Ventricular wall
structures.description: Muscle surrounding the ventricles contracts to pump blood.

structures.name: Interventricular septum
structures.description: The muscular partition separates the ventricles. No independent source mesh is available here.

structures.name: Tricuspid valve
structures.description: Between right atrium and right ventricle; helps prevent backward flow.

structures.name: Mitral valve
structures.description: Between left atrium and left ventricle; helps prevent backward flow.

structures.name: Pulmonary valve
structures.description: Between right ventricle and pulmonary trunk.

structures.name: Aortic valve
structures.description: Between left ventricle and aorta.

structures.name: Aorta
structures.description: Carries oxygen-rich blood into the systemic circulation.

structures.name: Superior vena cava
structures.description: Returns blood from the upper body to the right atrium.

structures.name: Inferior vena cava
structures.description: Returns blood from the lower body to the right atrium.

structures.name: Pulmonary trunk and arteries
structures.description: Carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs.

structures.name: Pulmonary veins
structures.description: Return oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

structures.name: Coronary arteries
structures.description: Supply the heart muscle itself.

conditions.name: Aortic dissection
conditions.summary: Blood enters the wall of the aorta and separates its layers. Location, extent and treatment differ between cases.
symptoms: Sudden severe chest or back pain
conditions.treatment: The existing exhibit shows true and false lumens. Repair may replace an affected segment or exclude an entry tear in selected cases; no universal repair is implied.

conditions.name: Coronary artery disease
conditions.summary: Plaque can narrow coronary arteries and limit blood supply to heart muscle.
conditions.treatment: Risk-factor care, medicines and selected procedures address different aspects of disease.

conditions.name: Myocardial infarction
conditions.summary: A sudden loss of blood supply can damage heart muscle. The highlighted wall is context, not an individual infarct map.
conditions.treatment: Emergency treatment aims to restore blood supply and limit injury.

conditions.name: Heart failure
conditions.summary: The heart cannot fill or pump adequately for the body’s needs. Different forms have different mechanisms.
conditions.treatment: Medicines, lifestyle support and selected devices or procedures depend on the type of heart failure.

conditions.name: Aortic stenosis
conditions.summary: A narrowed aortic valve obstructs outflow from the left ventricle.
conditions.treatment: Severe symptomatic disease may require valve replacement; medicines do not remove the valve obstruction.

conditions.name: Mitral regurgitation
conditions.summary: Incomplete mitral valve closure allows blood to leak backward during ventricular contraction.
conditions.treatment: Management depends on the cause and severity and may include valve repair or replacement.

brain.name: Brain
brain.referenceNote: Shared BodyParts3D adult-male organ reference, opened from either body. This is not a sex-specific organ reconstruction.

structures.name: Frontal lobe
structures.description: Participates in planning, movement and other functions within distributed networks.

structures.name: Parietal lobe
structures.description: Participates in body sensation and spatial processing.

structures.name: Temporal lobe
structures.description: Participates in hearing, memory and language-related networks.

structures.name: Occipital lobe
structures.description: Contains important visual-processing regions.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.description: Contributes to motor coordination and learning.

structures.name: Brainstem
structures.description: Connects brain and spinal cord and supports vital autonomic functions.

structures.name: Thalamus
structures.description: Participates in relaying and integrating information across brain networks.

structures.name: Hypothalamus
structures.description: Helps regulate internal balance, hormones and autonomic functions.

structures.name: Hippocampus
structures.description: Participates in learning and memory formation alongside connected regions.

structures.name: Amygdala
structures.description: Participates in emotion-related learning and processing, within broader networks.

structures.name: Basal ganglia
structures.description: Contribute to movement and learning through interconnected circuits.

structures.name: Corpus callosum
structures.description: A major white-matter connection between the cerebral hemispheres.

structures.name: Cerebral arteries
structures.description: Major arteries supply brain tissue. This surface model is not a verified flow network.

conditions.name: Brain tumors
conditions.summary: Brain tumors are abnormal growths of cells, with many different types and locations. The linked MRI example is a glioma research case; it does not represent all brain tumors.
symptoms: Changes in movement, vision or thinking can occur
conditions.treatment: Treatment depends on tumor type, location and individual clinical information. Surgery, radiation and systemic drug therapy are different categories; an MRI label alone cannot select among them. No tumor-specific drug record is currently in this catalog.

conditions.name: Alzheimer’s disease
conditions.summary: Alzheimer’s involves changes in proteins, synapses and neurons across networks. Its course varies between individuals.
symptoms: Changes in thinking and daily function
conditions.treatment: Symptom-directed medicines and selected early-disease amyloid therapies address different mechanisms. Eligibility and monitoring require specialist assessment.

conditions.name: Parkinson’s disease
conditions.summary: Loss of dopamine-producing neurons disrupts movement circuits. Highlighted structures are circuit context, not an exact lesion map.
conditions.treatment: Dopamine-related medicines, rehabilitation and selected procedures can help symptoms. Dedicated medicines are not yet in this catalog.

conditions.name: Ischemic stroke
conditions.summary: An arterial blockage reduces blood supply to part of the brain. Effects depend on the territory and duration.
conditions.treatment: Emergency assessment identifies candidates for clot-dissolving medicine or clot retrieval. Alteplase is a catalog example, not appropriate for every stroke.

conditions.name: Hemorrhagic stroke
conditions.summary: Bleeding in or around the brain can injure tissue and raise pressure. This model does not show an individual hemorrhage.
conditions.treatment: Emergency care differs from ischemic stroke; clot-dissolving drugs do not treat brain bleeding.

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.summary: Recurrent seizures arise from abnormal electrical activity in brain networks. Many different regions and causes can be involved.
conditions.treatment: Antiseizure medicines and selected non-drug approaches can help. Highlighted lobes are examples, not exclusive origins.

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis
conditions.summary: Immune-mediated injury affects myelin and nerve fibers in the central nervous system. Brain and spinal cord involvement varies.
conditions.treatment: Disease-modifying therapy differs from symptom relief. Baclofen in this catalog addresses spasticity; it does not modify the disease.

disabledCapabilities.name: Cerebral perfusion animation
disabledCapabilities.reason: No verified connected centerlines and flow directions.

exhibit.title: Healthy anatomy
exhibit.text: Explore a reference brain. This teaching model is not a diagnostic scan.

exhibit.title: Memory networks
exhibit.text: The hippocampus participates in memory alongside connected regions. Complex functions belong to networks.

exhibit.title: Amyloid and tau
exhibit.text: At microscopic scale, amyloid can accumulate between neurons and abnormal tau within them. This diagram is symbolic, not to scale.

exhibit.title: Synapses and neurons
exhibit.text: Disrupted communication and neuronal dysfunction affect networks. Moving markers represent a concept, not measured activity.

exhibit.title: Regional vulnerability
exhibit.text: Memory-related regions may be affected early, with broader involvement over time. Highlights do not predict an individual’s progression.

exhibit.title: Treatment mechanisms
exhibit.text: Cholinesterase inhibitors and an NMDA-receptor antagonist address symptoms. Amyloid-targeting antibodies can slow decline in selected early disease, with risks and monitoring needs.
